verses.1: When his army was being struck from behind by Padmanabha, Malvan then turned back, like the ocean reaching its shore.
verses.2: With bloodshot eyes from anger and a trembling crown, the demon spoke these words to Padmanabha, the best of men.
verses.3: O Narayana, you do not know the ancient duty of a warrior, as you kill us, who are frightened and not intent on fighting, like a common person.
verses.4: Whoever, not being a demon, commits the sin of killing those who have turned their back, that killer does not attain the heaven of those who perform meritorious deeds.
verses.5: Or if you have a desire for battle, O holder of conch, discus, and mace, I am standing here; show me the strength that is yours.
verses.6: The powerful younger brother of Indra, seeing Malyavan standing like an immovable mountain, spoke to that king of Rakshasas.
verses.7: I indeed granted protection and the destruction of Rakshasas to the gods who were terrified of you, and that promise is now being fulfilled.
verses.8: Indeed, the welfare of the gods is dearer to me than my own life, and therefore I will kill you all, even if you hide in the lowest netherworld.
verses.9: The greatly enraged king of Rakshasas pierced the chest of the god of gods, whose eyes were like red lotuses, with a spear as he was speaking.
verses.10: The spear, released from Malyavan's arm with a bell-like sound, shone on Hari's chest like a flash of lightning in a cloud.
verses.11: Then, the lotus-eyed Vishnu, dear to the wielder of Shakti, drew out that very spear and hurled it, aiming at Malyavan.
verses.12: That spear, released from Govinda's hand, flew towards the demon as if thrown by Skanda, desiring to strike, just as Indra's thunderbolt strikes the Anjana mountain.
verses.13: That spear fell upon the broad chest of the king of demons, which was shining with many necklaces, just as a thunderbolt strikes a mountain peak.
verses.14: With his armor shattered by that spear, Malyavan fell into deep unconsciousness, but then regained consciousness and stood unmoving like a mountain.
verses.15: Then, seizing a black iron spear covered with many spikes, Malyavan firmly struck the god between his breasts.
verses.16: The demon, eager for battle, struck Vishnu (Upendra) with his fist and then retreated a bow's length.
verses.17: Then a great cry of "well done, well done" arose in the sky as the demon, having struck Vishnu, also struck Garuda.
verses.18: Enraged, Garuda then blew away the demon with the powerful wind from his wings, just as a strong wind scatters a heap of dry leaves.
verses.19: Seeing his elder brother (Malyavan) driven away by the wind from Garuda's wings, Sumali, along with his own forces, headed towards Lanka.
verses.20: Malyavan, the demon who was tossed up by the force of the wing-wind, also rejoined his forces and went towards Lanka, overcome with shame.
verses.21: O lotus-eyed one, those Rākṣasas were repeatedly defeated in battle by that Hari (Vishnu), having their chief leaders slain.
verses.22: Being unable to fight against Vishnu and afflicted by fear, they abandoned Lanka and went to dwell in Pātāla along with their wives.
verses.23: O best of Raghu's lineage, those Rākṣasas, renowned for their valor, joined the Rākṣasa Sumālin and settled in the lineage of Sālakaṭaṅkaṭa.
verses.24: The Rākṣasas of the Pulastya lineage whom you killed, O Rama, include Sumālī, Mālyavān, Mālī, and their other leaders.
verses.25: O highly fortunate one, all of them were more powerful than Rāvaṇa.
verses.26: No one else can kill the Rākṣasas, who are enemies and tormentors of the gods, except for the god Nārāyaṇa, who holds the conch, discus, and mace.
verses.27: You are indeed the eternal, four-armed god Nārāyaṇa, manifested to kill the Rākṣasas, and you are the unconquerable, imperishable lord.
verses.28: He, who is affectionate towards those who seek refuge, manifests from time to time to re-establish the lost order of Dharma, protect beings, and destroy villains.
verses.29: O King of men, I have today narrated to you the complete and proper origin of the Rākṣasas; now, O best of Raghu's lineage, listen further to the entire incomparable power and birth of Rāvaṇa along with his sons.
